nodes.label: Rajasekar 2022 PMC HTML
nodes.author: P. Rajasekar; J. A. V. Selvi

nodes.label: Electronic nose (eNose)
nodes.rationale: Partially selective gas-sensor array plus pattern recognition yields a multi-dimensional smell print for gas ID or concentration estimation.

nodes.label: Metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) sensor
nodes.rationale: Heated MOS resistance changes with reducing gases like CH4; low-cost but cross-sensitive to humidity/temperature and often nonlinear.

nodes.label: Delta-V (ΔV) feature extraction
nodes.rationale: Relative voltage change vs baseline (dV, dV_max, slope) reduces baseline drift versus raw ADC voltage alone.

nodes.label: Linear Regression for CH4 ppm
nodes.rationale: Interpretable, light enough for Raspberry Pi; may be insufficient if response is nonlinear or interactions are complex.

nodes.label: Static chamber + GC-FID ground truth
nodes.rationale: Accepted agricultural GHG reference; high accuracy but labor-intensive and low sampling frequency — used for training/validation not continuous field monitoring.

nodes.label: Anaerobic methanogenesis in paddy soils
nodes.rationale: Flooded anaerobic soils enable methanogens; CH4 exits via water surface, ebullition, and aerenchyma.

nodes.label: Baseline–Measure sequence
nodes.rationale: Separates reference flow from sample measure so relative signal change is comparable across cycles.

nodes.label: MOS cross-sensitivity
nodes.rationale: Humidity, temperature, and interferents can dominate CH4 response; compensate with T/H/P sensors and/or ML.

nodes.label: Research gap: eNose+ML+rice+chamber-GC
nodes.rationale: Prior work splits into eNose+ML for ambient CH4, MOS in paddies without ML, or ML on soil/water factors without eNose — no single study combines MOS array, ppm regression, and rice with chamber–GC validation.
